findings.description: Unsafe __import__() call in find_python_module() enables arbitrary code execution via YAML deserialization
findings.reasoning: The __import__() call at line 531 is used to dynamically import arbitrary Python modules when unsafe=True. This is called by UnsafeConstructor.find_python_module() which is invoked during YAML deserialization of python/module tags. An attacker can craft malicious YAML that imports arbitrary modules, potentially leading to code execution if those modules have side effects during import. While this is intentionally part of the UnsafeConstructor API, it represents a critical vulnerability when UnsafeConstructor or Loader (which inherits from UnsafeConstructor) is used with untrusted YAML input.

evidence.dataflow_analysis: The unsafe parameter is set to True by UnsafeConstructor.find_python_module() at line 716. This method is called during YAML deserialization when processing python/module tags. The __import__() function can execute arbitrary code if the imported module has side effects.
evidence.notes: This is part of the PyYAML library's intentional unsafe deserialization support. The vulnerability exists because UnsafeConstructor and the default Loader class enable arbitrary code execution through YAML deserialization.
